title: Boost memory records via bounded prior tie-break, not filtering
context: In a graph with thousands of indexed symbols, exploratory 'why' queries got buried under symbol matches sharing the query's vocabulary, causing memory records (the actual recorded intent) to disappear from top-k results entirely. Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex).
decision: Apply a bounded negative position shift (default 12) to memory-kind records (decisions, constraints, bugs, runbooks, policies) to break vocabulary ties in favor of intent, without filtering—symbols remain fully reachable for name-based lookups.
consequences: Memory records now surface in 'why' queries despite vocabulary overlap with symbols (measured: Recall@10 70%→90%, MRR 0.402→0.575)
The shift is applied outside the main ranking clamp to prevent it from becoming the primary sort key—preserves that trust-based ranking remains the main signal
Symbol queries and structure lookups unaffected: symbols stay reachable, the prior only breaks ties between kinds
alternatives_rejected: Hard filtering (exclude symbols from results): breaks symbol-name queries and hunch_structure-style lookups that explicitly want code results
Semantic ranking only: doesn't address the lexical vocabulary-overlap tie problem where symbols and decisions compete for the same top-k slots
Accept 70% recall as-is: insufficient for reliable intent discovery in large graphs
